# Breadcrumbs

The trail from the site's root to the current page.

```tsx
import { Breadcrumbs } from "@rata/react";
```

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `breadcrumbs` |
| Family | navigation |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | latest / latest / future |
| Depends on | — |

## Props

Extends `Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLElement>, "aria-label">`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `items` | `BreadcrumbsItem[]` | — | The trail in order, root first. The last item is the current page and is not a link. |
| `label?` | `string` | `"Breadcrumb"` | Accessible name for the navigation landmark. |
| `separator?` | `ReactNode` | `"/"` | What sits between crumbs. |

### `items`

```ts
items: BreadcrumbsItem[]
```

The trail in order, root first. The last item is the current page and is not a link.

Source doc: The trail in order, root first. The last item is the current page.

**Use when**

- Every ancestor of the current page, ending with the page itself.

**Don't use for**

- Omitting the current page. The trail ends at where you are; ending it at the parent leaves the reader unsure whether the last crumb is a link they are already on.
- A trail that is not a hierarchy. Breadcrumbs say where this page sits, not how the user got here — history is the back button's job.
- Giving the last item an `href`. It is the page you are on, and this component drops it.

**Accessibility** Rendered as an ordered list inside a `<nav>`, so the count and the order are announced. The last item gets `aria-current="page"` and renders as text rather than a link.

### `label`

```ts
label?: string = "Breadcrumb"
```

Accessible name for the navigation landmark.

**Use when**

- Changing it only when a page has more than one navigation landmark and they need telling apart.

**Accessibility** Becomes the `<nav>`'s `aria-label`. A page with several landmarks needs distinct names or they are indistinguishable in a landmark list.

### `separator`

```ts
separator?: ReactNode = "/"
```

What sits between crumbs.

**Don't use for**

- A character that carries meaning, such as an arrow implying a flow. The separator is punctuation.

**Accessibility** Decorative and `aria-hidden`: the list structure already conveys the order, and announcing 'slash' between every crumb is noise.

## Use cases

### A page three levels deep

The ordinary case.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs
  items={[
    { label: "Home", href: "/" },
    { label: "Reports", href: "/reports" },
    { label: "Q3 revenue" },
  ]}
/>
```

The last item has no `href` — it is the page you are on. It renders as text with `aria-current="page"` rather than a link to itself.

### One landmark among several

A page that also has a primary nav and a pagination nav.

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs label="Breadcrumb" items={trail} />
```

Distinct `aria-label`s are what make landmarks tellable apart in a screen reader's landmark list. Two navs both called 'Navigation' are worse than one.

## Real usage in this repo

```tsx
<Breadcrumbs
        label="Breadcrumb"
        items={[
          { label: "Settings", href: "#" },
          { label: "Billing" },
        ]}
      />
```

## Token recipe

### base

A trail of links ending in the current page.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| gap between crumbs | `space.gap.xs` |
| font-size | `type.supporting.size — a trail is orientation, not content, so it sits below body size` |
| link color | `theme.accent-role.fg — the token documented for an inline link` |
| current page color | `theme.fg.primary — the end of the trail is where you are, so it reads as text rather than as another link` |
| current page font-weight | `type.control.weight` |
| separator color | `theme.fg.muted — punctuation, quieter than either crumb` |
| outline (focus-visible) | `focus.ring-width solid theme.focus-ring, offset focus.ring-offset` |
| transition | `motion.interactive.duration with motion.interactive.easing` |
